title: Find the Sum of the Power of All Subsequences
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n and a positive integer k, calculate the total number of subsequences whose sum equals k, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n and a positive integer k, calculate the total number of subsequences whose sum equals k, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: nums contains positive integers and k is positive.
For every subsequence T of nums, its power is the number of subsequences of T whose sum equals k.
Return the sum of those powers modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def sum_of_subsequence_powers(nums,k):
    modulo=1000000007;dp=[0]*(k+1);dp[0]=1
    for value in nums:
        following=[count*2%modulo for count in dp]
        for total in range(value,k+1):following[total]=(following[total]+dp[total-value])%modulo
        dp=following
    return dp[k]

def sum_of_subsequence_powers(nums,k):
    modulo=1000000007;dp=[0]*(k+1);dp[0]=1
    for value in nums:
        following=[count*2%modulo for count in dp]
        for total in range(value,k+1):following[total]=(following[total]+2*dp[total-value])%modulo
        dp=following
    return dp[k]

Use sum-indexed DP where skipping the current value doubles existing power and selecting it adds the prior lower-sum power once.
next[sum]=2*dp[sum]; when sum≥value add dp[sum-value], all modulo the required prime.
Every nested pair (target subset, containing outer subsequence) uniquely either omits the current element from both or selects it into the target subset, matching the two transitions.
